title: quant-eval-slice-regression-notes-wip
content:
Summary:

This is a working note capturing the latest quantization impact evaluations on candidate model variants (base fp16 -> int8, int4, AWQ, GPTQ) for onboarding into Redwood's serving catalog. The goal: produce slice-level quality deltas, document failure modes, and propose pass/fail gating for production rollouts (hosted + dedicated).

High-level takeaways (short):
- int8 variants generally maintain instruction-following and summarization quality within a 0–2% delta on automated metrics for most slices, but show occasional tokenization regressions on long-context QA (> 2k tokens).
- int4 (naive) exhibits larger variance: good on short conversational prompts, significant drop (-4% to -12%) on coding and factual QA slices.
- AWQ profiles (mixed-width quantization) often match or exceed naive int4 in throughput and keep quality deltas near int8 for key slices; failure cases concentrated on arithmetic reasoning and chain-of-thought style prompts.
- GPTQ (per-channel optimized) gave the best int4-like quality for many slices but is brittle on extremely low-entropy generation (few-shot codewith exact tokens).

Dataset / prompt sets used (short):
- Redwood-evals-core: 3k examples (instruction-following, summarization, classification).
- QA-long: 1.2k examples > 2k tokens context (customer KB style).
- Codex-lite: 1k coding prompts (python algos + unit-test checks).
- ReasonBench-subset: 800 arithmetic and multi-step reasoning prompts.
- Chat-PLG-sim: 2k short-turn chat prompts (memory + persona).

Slices defined for this report: each example is tagged by slice during inference so we can compute per-slice deltas.
- instruction-following (IF): generation quality measured by BLEU/ROUGE/ROUGE-L and human-ish heuristics (length-normalized).
- summarization (SUM): ROUGE-L, compression ratio, factuality spot-checks.
- long-context QA (LCQA): exact-match / F1 against gold drawn from KB.
- coding (CODE): pass@1 and unit-test pass rate.
- reasoning (REAS): answer accuracy on ReasonBench subset.
- chat-turn (CHAT): dialogue coherence + hallucination rate (heuristic matcher).

Metrics reported: automated metrics above plus token-level perplexity and model confidence (log-prob mass of top-k). Human evals were run for the 300 highest-delta cases per quantization method (summary later).

Evaluation methodology (notes / reproducibility):
- All variants run on identical input batches with seeds fixed at 42 where applicable.
- Beam width = 1, sampling temperature = 0.0 for deterministic comparisons where appropriate; sampling experiments done separately for chat-sim slice at t=0.7.
content_2:
- KV-cache preserved across variants (we validated that quantization didn't alter cache indexing).
- Pre/post-processing identical; tokenization consistent (same tokenizer binary).
- For AWQ and GPTQ we used the model-specific calibration set (500 random examples) to pick block sizes and scale factors; calibration logs are linked.

Numeric summary (automated metric deltas vs fp16 baseline):
- int8 (global):
  - IF: -0.8% ROUGE-L
  - SUM: -1.2% ROUGE-L
  - LCQA: -2.9% F1
  - CODE: -1.7% pass@1
  - REAS: -3.4% accuracy
  - CHAT: -0.9% coherence
- int4 (naive, per-tensor):
  - IF: -2.6%
  - SUM: -4.8%
  - LCQA: -11.2%
  - CODE: -9.5%
  - REAS: -12.0%
  - CHAT: -3.0%
- AWQ (per-channel mixed widths):
  - IF: -0.9%
  - SUM: -1.5%
  - LCQA: -3.6%
  - CODE: -2.1%
  - REAS: -5.9%
  - CHAT: -1.2%
- GPTQ (optimized int4):
  - IF: -1.0%
  - SUM: -2.3%
  - LCQA: -4.0%
  - CODE: -3.5%
  - REAS: -6.3%
  - CHAT: -1.1%

Notes on these numbers: they are medians across example-level deltas; there are long tails (see "worst-regressions" artifact). For LCQA and CODE the metric drops correlate with token probability drops in the first 30 tokens after the answer boundary.

Representative failure modes (concrete examples):
- LCQA: quantized variants often produce an answer anchored in the wrong document chunk when the gold answer spans a token boundary near a rare token. Example: KB article with id "kb-99X" — fp16 returns explicit paragraph, int4 returns paraphrase that misses the entity identifier.
- CODE: GPTQ-int4 variant misses specific function names or small punctuation (missing ':' or wrong indentation) causing unit tests to fail; often output contains off-by-one errors in loops.
- REAS: chain-of-thought style prompts where intermediate steps are needed — quantized variants sometimes drop justification steps but still output final answer, causing lower accuracy on step-sensitive benchmarks.

Human eval summary (300 highest-delta per-method):
- Sampling: raters given side-by-side fp16 vs quantized output blind. 3 raters per item, majority vote.
- int8: 5% of cases flagged as "noticeable regression"; of those, 60% were acceptable degradations (style or brevity), 40% were factual or correctness issues.
- AWQ/gptq: ~11% flagged; higher concentration in reasoning and code.
- int4: ~28% flagged; many unacceptable for prod in LCQA/CODE slices.

Operational throughput / perf notes (observed on internal bench):
- int8: 1.9x throughput vs fp16 on A100-like nodes (per our runtime). Latency improved proportionally for streaming endpoints.
- AWQ: 2.6x throughput for same fp32-attention kernels but memory footprint reduced more than int8 in some layers.
- GPTQ/int4: 3.2x throughput but with variance depending on kernel fusion; some sequences show 10–20% jitter.

Gating recommendations for onboarding (proposed):
1) Slice pass thresholds (relative to fp16): IF <= 2% ROUGE-L delta, SUM <= 3% delta, LCQA <= 3% F1 delta, CODE <= 2% pass@1 delta, REAS <= 4% accuracy delta.
2) Human-eval pass: no more than 8% of sampled items marked as "unacceptable regression" across slices marked critical (LCQA, CODE, REAS).
3) Edge-case tests: a curated set of 500 long-context KB queries must have <= 5% absolute EM loss.
4) Smoke tests for token-level consistency on punctuation-sensitive tasks (unit tests for code).

Recommendations / next steps (actionable):
- Short-term: promote int8 to experimental in hosted catalog (canary group: 5% of traffic, non-sensitive customers) with observability flags recording slice-level deltas.
- Medium-term: invest in GPTQ per-layer tuning for CODE and LCQA layers; try mixed AWQ+GPTQ hybrid for layers 6-10 where we see highest sensitivity.
- Calibration: expand calibration set to include 1k examples from customer KBs (with permission) to reduce LCQA tokenization edge cases.
- Monitoring: add automatic regression alerting if per-slice metric deltas exceed gating thresholds for any 1-hour window.

Open questions / TODOs (team discussion points):
- How to weight human-eval vs automated metrics when they disagree? Propose a tie-breaker: if human-eval flagged > 10% unacceptable but automated metrics within gating thresholds, fail onboarding.
- Can runtime fallbacks be more granular? e.g., route CODE and LCQA to fp16 while other slices use quantized model at inference time; need cost/latency sim.
- Need to expand prompt set diversity for AWQ calibration: current calibration examples underrepresent multi-lingual prompts.

Artifacts and where to look (quick links):
- worst-regressions.csv (artifact): lists top 5k example deltas by absolute change.
- calibration-logs/awq-2026-02-01.log
- perf-bench/throughput-compare-2026-03-07.csv
- human-eval-folder: s3://redwood-inference-evals/quant-human/2026-03
- notebook: github:repo/model-quant-eval/notebooks/analysis.ipynb

Notes to reviewers (please):
- Focus review on LCQA and CODE slices — these are the highest-risk for customer-facing regressions.
- Flag any suspicious calibration parameters (e.g., block size < 4 on first layers).
- Suggest additional prompt slices we should include before finalizing gating (I suspect multi-turn retrieval QA and multilingual instructions are missing).

Rough timeline suggestion:
- Week 0 (now): open PR for int8 canary config + observability dashboards
- Week 1–2: run canary, collect metrics, expand calibration if LCQA delta > 3%
- Week 3: decision point for wider rollout or rollback

Choppy notes / quick observations (work-in-progress):
- saw weird tokenization at char boundary for emoji in chat-sim on AWQ; investigate tokenizer binary mismatch?
- GPTQ tuning gave large wins when we increased per-channel bit allocation for keys/values but slowed perf; tradeoff analysis pending.

Author note: this doc is intentionally conversational; please annotate any items you want promoted into the formal onboarding checklist.

-- Aisha
